name: Tennant Creek
note: Town: the regional hub and gold-rush town on the Stuart Highway, the base for the Barkly region's sights (a destination candidate, not a spot).

name: Barkly Tableland
note: Region: the vast cattle-country plain between Tennant Creek and Queensland (a destination-name candidate, not a spot).

name: Devils Marbles
wiki: Karlu Karlu / Devils Marbles Conservation Reserve
note: Landscape: a conservation reserve of granite boulders balanced on one another, a sacred Warumungu site about 105 km south of Tennant Creek, with a walking path and camping.

name: The Pebbles
note: Landscape: granite rock formation 10 km north of Tennant Creek, known to the Warumungu as Kunjarra, a women's dancing site (Devils Pebbles).

name: Tennant Creek Telegraph Station
note: Historic site: 1872 stone telegraph station on the Overland Telegraph Line with a self-guided walk, 10 km north of town, free entry.

name: Nyinkka Nyunyu Art and Culture Centre
note: Museum and cultural centre: Warumungu art, culture and interpretive exhibits in the town centre, entry fee.

name: Battery Hill Mining Centre
coordinates_source: osm:tourism=museum (Battery Hill Mining Centre), resolve-pin HIGH
note: Museum: gold-mining heritage centre with underground tour and Australia's last operating ten-head gold stamp battery, in town. No Wikipedia article for the NT site (the Battery Hill article is the Queensland one).

name: Tennant Creek Museum
note: Museum: a WWII army hospital building (Tuxworth Fullwood House) holding gold-rush, police and telegraph exhibits and an early photo archive, entry fee.

name: Winanjjikari Music Centre
note: Cultural venue: Aboriginal musicians' centre in town where visitors can watch daily life and join in a song, free entry.

name: Bill Allen Lookout
note: Viewpoint: lookout just east of town with a 360-degree view over the town and landscape, best at sunset.

name: Lake Mary Ann
note: Recreation lake: 1980 dam 5 km north of Tennant Creek with swimming, canoeing, picnic grounds and a walking track through the Honeymoon Ranges (formerly Mary Ann Dam).

name: Warrego Fossicking Area
note: Activity: public gold-fossicking area 15 km from the small mining town of Warrego; a permit is needed (fossicking, not a formal attraction).

name: Banka Banka Station
note: Cattle station stay: historic mud-brick homestead, campground and cattle station 100 km north of Tennant Creek, first pastoral lease in the region.

name: Iytwelepenty / Davenport Range National Park
note: National park: rugged ranges east of Tennant Creek with 4WD tracks, permanent waterholes and rock wallabies, about 1,120 km2 (formerly Davenport Murchison National Park).

name: Old Police Station Waterhole
note: Swimming waterhole and campsite inside Davenport Range National Park, reached by 4WD track; the cold winter water is for summer swims.

name: Wycliffe Well
note: Landmark: self-proclaimed UFO capital of Australia, a roadhouse and caravan park on the Stuart Highway with UFO sighting logs and a sunrise and sunset draw.

name: Lake Wycliffe
note: Lake: man-made 10-acre recreational lake a 300 m walk from Wycliffe Well roadhouse.

name: Wycliffe Well Railway
note: Landmark: a relocated Victorian sugar-cane train on display at Wycliffe Well since 1998 (a static display).

name: Barrow Creek Telegraph Station
note: Historic site: 1872 stone telegraph station reserve on the Stuart Highway, with a self-guided walk through the original buildings.

name: Barrow Creek Hotel
note: Pub: historic 1926 pub and roadhouse with a tin ceiling, cellar and walls covered in visitors' messages and business cards (a venue; judge against the venue rule).

name: Barrow Creek
note: Town: tiny roadhouse settlement on the Stuart Highway, about 280 km north of Alice Springs, named after J. H. Barrow.

name: Threeways Roadhouse
note: Roadhouse: the junction of the Stuart and Barkly highways 80 km north of Tennant Creek, known for a painted road-train mural on its wall.

name: Renner Springs
note: Town: roadhouse and desert inn 150 km north of Tennant Creek with a short lagoon and springs walk.

name: Newcastle Waters
note: Ghost town: preserved historic buildings (Jones's Store, the Junction Hotel) and a drovers' memorial off the Explorers Way, 282 km north of Tennant Creek.

name: Elliott
note: Town: roadhouse town on the Stuart Highway at the halfway point between Darwin and Alice Springs, with a post office, police station and clinic.

name: Attack Creek Historical Reserve
note: Historic reserve: a 0.22 ha site 74 km north of Tennant Creek with the Stuart memorial cairn and etchings marking John McDouall Stuart's 1860 expedition, free and open all hours.

name: Barkly Homestead
note: Roadhouse: fuel, caravan park and gravel airstrip at the Barkly Highway and Tablelands Highway junction (a service stop).

name: Heartbreak Hotel
note: Roadhouse: the Heartbreak Hotel at the Carpentaria and Tablelands highway junction, base for Lost City helicopter flights (Cape Crawford area). Coordinates are the Cape Crawford locality point, not the hotel; fix from OSM.

name: Cape Crawford Lost City
note: Landscape: sandstone formations of the Lost City in Limmen National Park, reached by helicopter from Heartbreak Hotel near Cape Crawford (not the Litchfield Lost City).

name: Connells Lagoon Conservation Reserve
note: Wildlife reserve: wetland with several rare and endangered birds between Brunette Downs and Alexandria Station, reached by unsealed road in a 2WD.

name: Brunette Downs
note: Cattle station: a 12,000 km2 pastoral lease on the Tablelands Highway with no public visitor facilities (station, not a place to go).

name: Anmatjere Man
note: Landmark: 12 m steel-and-cement sculpture of an Anmatjere man beside the Stuart Highway at Aileron Roadhouse, with a companion woman and child figure and a nearby Aileron sign.

name: Ti-Tree
note: Town: small service town (roadhouse and store) on the Stuart Highway north of Alice Springs, a locality of about 90 people (edge of the region).
